articles.title: Delhi Lakshmi Yojana Portal Goes Live, Offers Women Rs 2,500 Monthly Aid
articles.excerpt: The BJP-led Delhi government's flagship welfare scheme launches its online registration portal on August 1, targeting lakhs of eligible women ahead of a Raksha Bandhan rollout.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with family in Delhi may need to verify whether female relatives qualify, given the strict residency and income criteria that could exclude middle-class households.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UEFA Declares Loss of Confidence in FIFA President Infantino Over World Cup Sell-Off
articles.excerpt: European soccer's governing body delivered its sharpest rebuke of Gianni Infantino after FIFA was forced to abandon a $4.2 billion plan to sell private stakes in the World Cup.
articles.nri_angle: The governance crisis at FIFA may affect how major tournaments like the World Cup are commercialized and broadcast, relevant to millions of Indian soccer fans worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Game Developers Launch Itch.io Bundle to Fund Relief for Laid-Off Workers
articles.excerpt: The Game Industry Hardship Fund bundle, organized by Necrosoft Games and the United Videogame Workers union, offers over 100 DRM-free games for $10 with all proceeds supporting laid-off developers in the US and Canada.
articles.nri_angle: South Asian game industry professionals on employer-sponsored visas face heightened vulnerability during layoffs, making peer-driven hardship funds especially relevant.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: China Overtakes U.S. in Global Popularity, but India Remains a Rare Pro-American Holdout
articles.excerpt: A Pew Research Center survey of 36 countries finds China is now viewed more favorably than the United States for the first time in two decades — but India, alongside just five other nations, still backs Washington.
articles.nri_angle: India is one of only six countries that still views the U.S. more favorably than China, a position shaped by border tensions with Beijing that directly affects how the diaspora navigates great-power competition abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Thousands March Down Kyiv's Khreshchatyk Demanding Ousted Defence Minister's Return
articles.excerpt: Protesters flood Ukraine's main boulevard in the largest rally yet against President Zelenskiy's decision to dismiss Mykhailo Fedorov, the tech-savvy reformer credited with transforming the country's wartime military.
articles.nri_angle: Sustained protests in wartime Ukraine highlight democratic governance under pressure, a dynamic closely watched by global observers including Indian analysts monitoring the war's geopolitical fallout.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Student Abroad Reveals Losing 10 Kilos as Falling Rupee Makes Basic Living Unaffordable
articles.excerpt: A viral blog post captures the hidden cost of the rupee's slide past 90 to the dollar, as Indian students abroad face soaring expenses, top-up loan demands, and deteriorating living conditions.
articles.image_caption: The Indian rupee has slid past 90 to the US dollar, sharply increasing the cost of living and education for Indian students abroad.
articles.nri_angle: Directly impacts Indian students and families funding overseas education as the rupee's slide past 90/dollar reshapes affordability and destination choices.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nearly Half of NRI Property Owners in India Want to Sell, Survey Finds
articles.excerpt: A Business Standard survey reveals growing NRI disenchantment with Indian real estate as tax changes, low rental yields, and overseas alternatives drive a sell-off sentiment.
articles.nri_angle: Directly affects millions of NRIs who own property in India and are reassessing their holdings amid unfavorable tax changes and low yields.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NASA's Curiosity Rover Photographs a Vast 'Sea of Polygons' on Mars That 'Took Our Breath Away'
articles.excerpt: The rover discovered the largest field of honeycomb-like fracture patterns ever found on Mars while exploring Valle Grande, offering new clues about the planet's ancient watery past.
articles.nri_angle: Indian scientists at ISRO have their own Mars exploration legacy with the Mangalyaan mission, and discoveries like these inform the global understanding of planetary science.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rocky 'Super-Earth' 49 Light-Years Away Shows First Signs of Atmosphere, Boosting Search for Alien Life
articles.excerpt: Scientists have detected helium escaping from LHS 1140b, a rocky planet in the habitable zone of its star, making it the strongest candidate yet for an atmosphere on an Earth-like world beyond our solar system.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin scientists have been prominent in exoplanet research, and the discovery opens new frontiers for international collaboration in space science.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian American Scholar Roopika Risam Makes Obama's 2026 Summer Reading List
articles.excerpt: Dartmouth professor's book 'Data Empire,' an 11,000-year history of how information shaped power, joins works by Colson Whitehead and Ann Patchett on Obama's annual picks.
articles.nri_angle: Roopika Risam's inclusion on Obama's reading list is a milestone for Indian American scholars, highlighting the growing influence of South Asian voices in mainstream American intellectual life.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Former Indian Army Chief General VN Sharma Dies at 96
articles.excerpt: General Vishwa Nath Sharma, the first president's commissioned officer to lead the Indian Army, served as Chief of Army Staff from 1988 to 1990 and stood firm during the 1987 Wangdung crisis with China.
articles.nri_angle: General Sharma's family represents a storied lineage of military service central to India's national identity, connecting generations of the diaspora to the country's post-independence military history.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Bid to Become a Global Education Hub Faces a Reality Check
articles.excerpt: Despite ambitious targets under the National Education Policy 2020, India hosts just 72,000 foreign students — a fraction of what rivals attract — and the gap between policy rhetoric and campus reality remains wide.
articles.image_caption: An Indian Institute of Technology campus. India aims to attract more international students but faces challenges including slow visa processing and limited infrastructure.
articles.nri_angle: India's struggle to attract foreign students contrasts with the massive outbound flow of Indian students to Western universities, raising questions about educational reciprocity and whether reforms can slow the brain drain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Wife of International Kabaddi Player Found Dead in Haryana, Dowry Harassment Alleged
articles.excerpt: The 23-year-old woman's family has accused her husband and in-laws of mental and physical harassment, with police registering a case under dowry death provisions.
articles.nri_angle: The case reignites discussion among the Indian diaspora about the persistence of dowry-related violence in India, a practice that continues despite decades of legislation and awareness campaigns.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US and Israel Planning Bombing Campaign Against Iranian Energy Infrastructure
articles.excerpt: Strikes on energy targets could begin as early as this weekend, CBS News reports, marking a significant escalation in the five-month-old conflict.
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans with family in the Gulf face growing disruption as the US-Iran conflict threatens regional energy markets and the safety of the large Indian expatriate community in the Middle East.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Federal Plan Mandates Steep Colorado River Water Cuts for California, Arizona and Nevada
articles.excerpt: The Bureau of Reclamation's 10-year framework requires lower basin states to slash water use by up to 20% as reservoirs hit record lows, with deeper cuts possible through 2036.
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans concentrated in Phoenix, Las Vegas and Southern California metro areas face water use restrictions and likely rate hikes as the federal government mandates steep cuts to Colorado River allocations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Faces Mounting Frustration as Iran Resists Deal and Advisors Clash on Path Forward
articles.excerpt: With Saudi Arabia urging de-escalation and Israel pushing for intensified pressure, President Trump confronts deepening divisions among allies and his own team over the five-month-old Iran conflict.
articles.image_caption: Camp David, where Trump met with advisors amid growing frustration over stalled Iran nuclear talks.
articles.nri_angle: The prolonged US-Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption are driving up energy prices globally, directly impacting NRIs in Gulf countries and Indian trade routes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Israel Heads to First Post-October 7 Election With Netanyahu's Grip on Power in Doubt
articles.excerpt: Israelis will vote on October 27 in a parliamentary election shaped by the Gaza war, with former military chief Gadi Eisenkot emerging as the prime minister's most serious challenger in years.
articles.nri_angle: India-Israel defence and tech partnerships could shift with a new government, and tens of thousands of Indian workers in Israel face direct stakes in the election's outcome.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Taslima Nasrin Set to Return to Kolkata After 19 Years of Exile
articles.excerpt: The exiled Bangladeshi author will attend a literary event at Rabindra Sadan on August 1, with West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari expected to share the stage in what organisers call a celebration of free speech.
articles.nri_angle: Nasrin's return tests India's commitment to free speech and secularism — issues that resonate deeply with the global Indian and Bengali diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pakistan to Host 2027 SCO Summit in Islamabad, Raising Question of Modi Visit
articles.excerpt: As Pakistan prepares to host the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit next year, diplomatic observers are watching whether India-Pakistan tensions will prevent PM Modi from attending.
articles.nri_angle: The India-Pakistan diplomatic trajectory affects regional security perceptions, travel, and trade corridors for the Indian diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Hamas Agrees to Gaza Disarmament Framework but Demands Israel Act First
articles.excerpt: Trump hails the Board of Peace deal as a milestone, but a standoff over sequencing — who disarms and who withdraws first — threatens to stall implementation.
articles.nri_angle: The Gaza framework has implications for regional stability, energy markets, and safety of Indian workers across the Middle East.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: FIFA Defiant Over $20 Billion World Cup Investment Plan Despite UEFA's Unanimous Boycott Vote
articles.excerpt: FIFA says it will press ahead with consultations on selling stakes in World Cup competitions even as Europe, CONCACAF, and the Asian Football Confederation unite in opposition.
articles.nri_angle: India's football federation, part of the Asian Football Confederation that has rejected FIFA's proposal, stands to lose or gain from the outcome of this governance battle that could reshape how World Cup revenues are distributed to developing football nations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Hyderabad Police Register Case Against Meta India Head Over Anti-Modi Facebook Videos
articles.excerpt: The FIR escalates a rapidly deteriorating relationship between the Modi government and Meta, coming days after India summoned the company's executives over an inadvertent restriction on a prime ministerial Facebook post.
articles.nri_angle: The standoff between India's government and Meta carries direct implications for how Indian diaspora communities use Facebook and Instagram to follow developments back home, particularly around politically sensitive content during periods of unrest.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Five Indians Arrested in Thailand for Kidnapping Three Indian Tourists in Pattaya
articles.excerpt: The victims were lured with a fake tour package, held captive for days, and subjected to staged torture as their captors demanded ransom — all allegedly directed by a Dubai-based Pakistani national.
articles.nri_angle: Indian tourists increasingly targeted in Southeast Asian kidnapping schemes; raises consular protection concerns for the growing Indian traveler population in Thailand.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IndiGo's Bhatia Slams India's Pilot Duty Rules as 'Uncompetitive,' Seeks Review
articles.excerpt: IndiGo managing director Rahul Bhatia has called for an overhaul of India's flight duty time rules, arguing they erode cockpit productivity and drive up airline costs—months after the regulations triggered the worst scheduling crisis in Indian aviation history.
articles.nri_angle: IndiGo's aggressive international expansion—including new long-haul routes to the UK, Europe, and plans for A350 widebody service—could offer diaspora travellers more direct, competitively priced connections to India, but regulatory and operational challenges remain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Russian Missile Lands in Poland as Overnight Strikes Kill Nine Across Ukraine
articles.excerpt: A suspected Russian Kh-101 cruise missile crashed in eastern Poland, prompting NATO scrambles, as Russia launched more than 70 missiles and 280 drones targeting cities from Kyiv to Lviv.
articles.nri_angle: Expanding Russian strikes into NATO territory raise security concerns for the large Indian diaspora population across Europe.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Parliament Clears Tougher Anti-Paper Leak Law After NEET Crisis
articles.excerpt: Both houses of Parliament have passed the Public Examinations Amendment Bill 2026, introducing up to 10 years' imprisonment and ₹50 lakh fines for exam fraud, as PM Modi vows to dismantle the 'paper mafia.'
articles.nri_angle: For millions of Indian students preparing for competitive exams that shape career pathways domestically and abroad, the tougher law and Nilekani-led technology reforms aim to restore trust in an examination system central to their aspirations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Dhanush's Political Buzz Grows After Fan Club Flag and Birthday Speech on Public Service
articles.excerpt: The Tamil superstar urged fans to focus on community welfare over film celebrations, fuelling comparisons with Vijay's political rise — though no official announcement has been made.
articles.image_caption: Dhanush, the Tamil actor and filmmaker whose fan club flag at a political rally has sparked speculation about his political ambitions.
articles.nri_angle: Tamil cinema stars entering politics shapes governance for millions; diaspora Tamils follow these developments closely given their cultural and family ties.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UN Warns 300,000 People Trapped in Asian Scam Centres as Trafficking Surges
articles.excerpt: The IOM says victims from India, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka are among those lured by fake job ads on social media and forced into criminal operations across Cambodia, Laos and Myanmar.
articles.nri_angle: Indians are explicitly named among the nationalities most targeted by trafficking networks, with English-fluent, university-educated job-seekers particularly vulnerable to fake employment ads funnelling them into scam compounds across Southeast Asia.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Deadly 7.1-Magnitude Earthquake Strikes Southern Japan, Killing at Least 13 With Dozens Still Missing
articles.excerpt: A powerful quake in Kumamoto prefecture triggered a massive explosion at the region's largest shopping mall, collapsed bridges and buildings, and forced the evacuation of over 10,000 people.
articles.nri_angle: Thousands of Indians live and work in Japan, particularly in manufacturing and IT, and a Vietnamese factory worker was among the dead — raising concerns for all foreign workers in the affected region.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Maldives Joins Bangladesh in Pushing for SAARC Revival as Muizzu Offers to Bridge India-Pakistan Divide
articles.excerpt: President Muizzu used the Maldives' Independence Day address to call on South Asian nations to resume dialogue, with the regional bloc dormant since 2016.
articles.nri_angle: SAARC revival could reshape trade, travel and cultural ties across South Asia, directly affecting diaspora communities from all eight member nations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Keigo Higashino, Japanese Mystery Master Beloved Across Asia, Dies at 68
articles.excerpt: The author of The Devotion of Suspect X — adapted into the Netflix India hit Jaane Jaan — died of colorectal cancer on July 23, leaving behind a body of work that reshaped crime fiction across continents.
articles.nri_angle: Higashino's Devotion of Suspect X was adapted into the Netflix India hit Jaane Jaan, connecting his storytelling directly to Indian audiences worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: China Wins Two Fields Medals in Historic First, Raising Questions About Global Math Education
articles.excerpt: Hong Wang and Yu Deng became the first Chinese nationals to win math's highest honor, but both trained in the U.S. — a fact that complicates China's victory lap and raises broader questions about where talent is cultivated.
articles.nri_angle: India's math talent pipeline mirrors China's — strong domestic olympiad performance but no Fields Medal — raising parallel questions about institutional support.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Eyes Entry Into GCAP Fighter Jet Program as Consortium Sets Deadline for New Partners
articles.excerpt: Leonardo CEO Lorenzo Mariani says new countries must commit within a year as India confirms interest in joining the UK-Japan-Italy sixth-generation stealth fighter project.
articles.nri_angle: India's potential entry into GCAP could reshape defense procurement partnerships and offer Indian defense manufacturers opportunities in a multinational program alongside the UK, Japan, and Italy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Puts Bihar's Plastic-to-Bench Recycling Model on National Stage
articles.excerpt: During his 136th Mann Ki Baat address, PM Modi highlighted how Sitamarhi district turns 40 kg of single-use plastic waste into durable benches for schools and parks.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised Sitamarhi district's plastic-to-bench recycling initiative during the 136th Mann Ki Baat broadcast.
articles.nri_angle: The commercially sustainable recycling model may interest diaspora investors and waste-tech entrepreneurs looking at circular economy opportunities in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Flex CEO Revathi Advaithi Pledges $1 Million for Women's Scholarships at BITS Pilani
articles.excerpt: The Indian American business leader and her husband announced a permanent endowment for women students from economically weaker backgrounds during the institute's 2026 convocation.
articles.image_caption: Revathi Advaithi, CEO of Flex, announced a $1 million scholarship endowment at her alma mater BITS Pilani.
articles.nri_angle: Indian American CEO channels personal journey as an immigrant engineer into philanthropy supporting women's education at her alma mater in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Faces Diplomatic Marathon With SCO, BRICS, and UNGA Summits in Six-Week Sprint
articles.excerpt: From Bishkek to New Delhi to New York, the Indian PM will navigate a packed global calendar that tests India's balancing act between rival power blocs.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi faces a packed diplomatic calendar with the SCO summit in Bishkek, the BRICS summit in New Delhi, and the UN General Assembly in rapid succession.
articles.nri_angle: India's diplomatic marathon at SCO, BRICS, and UNGA directly impacts diaspora through immigration policy, trade agreements, and geopolitical stability.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Who Is Shailesh Jejurikar? The Mumbai Boy Who Shared a Classroom With Satya Nadella — and Now Runs a $380 Billion American Giant
articles.image_caption: Shailesh Jejurikar, President and CEO of Procter & Gamble. He became the first Indian-born CEO of the company on January 1, 2026.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-Origin US Lawmakers Urge Diaspora to Enter Politics as Anti-India Hate Rises
articles.excerpt: At a Capitol Hill event, Congressmen Krishnamoorthi, Subramanyam and Thanedar called on Indian Americans to run for office at every level and fight back against a growing wave of anti-India rhetoric.
articles.image_caption: Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi speaks at a Capitol Hill event organized by the Foundation for India and Indian Diaspora Studies. The Illinois Democrat urged Indian Americans to run for office at every level to counter rising anti-India hate.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American lawmakers directly call on the diaspora community to enter politics to counter rising anti-India hate in the United States.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Diamond Trader Dhiru Ramani Freed in Mali After Family Pays €4 Million Ransom
articles.excerpt: The 75-year-old Surat businessman and two other Indian hostages were released after nearly three months in captivity; his family says it negotiated with the Al-Qaeda-linked group without government help.
articles.image_caption: Dhiru Ramani, a 75-year-old diamond businessman from Surat, was freed after nearly three months in captivity in Mali. His family reportedly paid a €4 million ransom to an Al-Qaeda-linked group.
articles.nri_angle: The kidnapping of an Indian businessman in Mali underscores the risks faced by diaspora entrepreneurs with operations in conflict-prone African nations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Punjabi Woman Navneet Kaur Shot Dead in Toronto, Brampton Man Charged With First-Degree Murder
articles.excerpt: Family alleges the accused, a married man, had been harassing and pressuring the 26-year-old to marry him. She had returned to Punjab months earlier out of fear before going back to Canada.
articles.nri_angle: The shooting of a 26-year-old Punjabi woman in Toronto adds to a troubling pattern of violence against Indian nationals in Canada, intensifying safety concerns across the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rhiya Ahir Pushes Back Against Online Smear Campaign After Iconic CJP Protest Moment
articles.excerpt: The 27-year-old Mumbai model and actress, who went viral for blocking a police van during CJP's anti-NEET protest, has addressed the wave of online abuse and misinformation targeting her since the incident.
articles.nri_angle: Ahir's stand has resonated with Indian-origin communities worldwide, drawing parallels to the Tiananmen Square 'Tank Man' and sparking diaspora conversations about civic courage and the cost of dissent in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
